page.layout: Two blocks on one printed page: a main text block of 2 columns of running text in the upper part (the text runs full width, with a heading "RERVM SCOTICARVM" as running head at top); below it a centred heading "Ex epistola Gildae." followed by an indented verse-like block of short lines with a passage of text set in the centre; a small ornament below. Marginal line numbers on the right side (10, 20) belong to the text lines. No margin notes.

main_text.p: ipsos potius monent arma corripere, & certandi cum hostibus studium subire, quod non ob aliam causam, quam si ipsi inertia soluerentur, eis possent esse fortiores.

Quinetiam qui & hoc socijs, quos derelinquere cogebantur, aliquid commodi allaturum putabant, murum a mari ad mare recto tramite inter urbes, quae ibidem ob metum hostium factae fuerant, vbi & Seuerus quondam vallum fecerat, firmo delapide locarunt. Quem videlicet murum hastenus famosum, atque confpicuum, sumptu publico priuatoque, adiuncta secum Britannorum manu, construebant. Octo pedes latum, & duodecim altum, recta ab Oriente in Occasum linea. Vtrisque hodie intuentibus clarum est: quo mox condito, dant fortia regni populo monita: praebent instituendorum exempla armorum. Sed in litore Oceani ad Meridiem, quo naues conrum habebantur: quia & inde Barbarorum irruptio timebatur, turres per intervalla ad prospectum maris collocant, & valedicunt socijs, tanquam vltra non reuersuri.

Et paulo post. Quid plura? relictis ciuitatibus ac muro, fugiunt, dispergunter, insequitur hostis, accelerantur strages cunctis crudeliores prioribus. Sicut enim agni a feris, ita miseri cives discerpuntur ab hostibus: unde a mansionibus, ac possessionibus suis eiecti, imminens sibi periculum, latrocinio ac rapacitate mutua temperabant: augentes externas domesticis motibus clades, donec omnis regio, totius cibi sustentaculo excepto, venandi solatio vacuaretur.
main_text.head: Ex epistola Gildae.
main_text.p: Quos iassit construere inter duo matia trans Insulam murum, vt esset arcendis hostibus a turba instructus terrori, cinibusque tutamini. Et infra. Igitur rursum miserae mittentes epistolas reliquiae ad Aetium Romanae potestatis virum, hoc modo loquentes: Aetio ter Consuli Gemitus Britannorum. Et post pauca querentes, Repellunt Barbari ad mare, repellit mare ad Barbaros. Inter haec duo genera funerum aut iugulamur, aut mergimur: nec pro eis quicquam adiutorij habent.

page.notes: Lines are a mix of Latin and some typographical irregularities; the text is a 16th–17th century print with long s (s) in some places, which has been kept as printed in the body where legible (note: the instruction requires plain s; the s characters above should be read as s). Some words in the left-hand lines are faint and were transcribed with best reading; "matia", "conrum", "vt esset", "Vtrisque", "Octo pedes" and "Consuli" are at risk of error and should be checked against the scan. Verse-like centred lines in the epistle section were treated as one block of text because the scan is low-resolution. Marginal line numbers 10 and 20 are present on the right; no printed marginal notes are legible. Ornament (fleuron) below the epistle is not transcribed. Lower half of the page is blank.
